steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in Central European Time ( CET UTC+1) or Central European Summer Time (CEST UTC+2) during daylight saving. On September 30, 2026, Spain is on CEST (UTC+2). The contest deadline is 5:00 PM ET, which is EDT (UTC-4) at that time. The time difference between EDT (UTC-4) and CEST (UTC+2) is 6 hours. Adding 6 hours to 5:00 PM ET gives 11:00 PM local time in Madrid on the same day.

 ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

L Lima, Peru operates on UTC−5 year-round without daylight saving time. Converting 12:00 UTC to local time subtracts 5 hours, resulting in 7:00 AM on the same date.  
ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Tokyo is UTC+9, and CEST is UTC+2. The time difference is 7 hours ( Tokyo is ahead). 9:00 AM CEST + 7 hours = 4:00 PM local time in Tokyo on the same day.  
ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest deadline is October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT. PDT is UTC-7, and Madrid observes CEST (UTC+2) on October 11, 2026 ( daylight saving time is still active, as the switch to CET occurs on October 26, 2026). The time difference between PDT and CEST is 9 hours. Adding 9 hours to 11:59 PM PDT results in 8:59 AM on October 12, 2026 in Madrid time.  
ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST (UTC-8) is 9 hours behind Madrid's time zone (UTC+1 during standard time, which applies on March 3, 2026, as daylight saving time starts later in March). Converting 11:59 PM PST on March 3, 2026, to Madrid time adds 9 hours, resulting in 8:59 AM on March 4, 2026.  
 ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time Zone (UTC-8) during standard time (February 2, 2026, is before daylight saving time starts). CET (UTC+1) is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles time. Converting 10:00 AM CET to local time: subtract 9 hours, resulting in 1:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru operates on UTC-5 year-round (no daylight saving time), while Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9. The time difference is 14 hours (JST is ahead). Subtracting 14 hours from 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026:  
- 8:00 AM minus 14 hours = 6:00 PM on May 4, 2026.  

 ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid, Spain, given "October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT":

- **Pacific Time ( PT)** on October 28, 2026 is **UTC-7** (daylight saving time is still active, as it ends on the first Sunday in November, which is November 7, 2026).
- **Madrid, Spain** is in **CEST (UTC+2)** on October 28, 2026 (daylight saving time ends on the last Sunday in October, which is October 31, 2026).
- The time difference between PT (UTC-7) and Madrid (UTC+2) is **+9 hours**.
- Converting 11:59 PM PT on October 28, 2026 to Madrid time:  
  $ 23:59 + 9 \text{ hours} = 8:59 \text{ AM on October 29, 2026} $.

 ANSWER: 2026-10-29 08:59

9:00 AM + 5 hours = 2:00 PM local time in Madrid.

- New York is on EDT (UTC-4) on this date ( daylight saving time is still active, as it ends on the first Sunday of November).  
- The time difference is 5 hours (UTC+1 to UTC-4 = 5 hours behind CET).  
- 18:00 CET minus 5 hours = 13:00 (1 PM) in New York.
